citation.title: Data assimilation system based on integrated transport simulation of Large Helical Device plasma
citation.authors: Morishita Y., Murakami S., Yokoyama M., Ueno G.

topic: EnKF data assimilation of measured Te, Ti and density profiles into TASK3D transport simulation of one LHD NBI shot
own_question: Can sequential Bayesian filtering jointly estimate temperatures, densities, turbulence-model coefficients and NBI deposition factors so that predictions track measured profiles?
actual_method_and_evidence: EnKF with 2000 members, 60 radial grid points, and gyro-Bohm models. Fitted, time-interpolated profiles from one LHD shot (114053) are assimilated every 80 or 160 ms. The paper reports qualitative agreement with measurements, coefficient estimates and correlations, and a log-likelihood that depends on ensemble size. The run takes about 5 hours on 2000 cores, so it is not real time. The Ti diagnostic is not specified in the extracted text. There is no held-out validation.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Sequential filtering (predict, then update with observations) has been used to fuse past fusion-plasma profile data into a model-based estimate, as background for causal estimation concepts.
claim_checks.qualification: This is an LHD physics-model EnKF run offline on a single shot. It does not use BES/ECEI, KSTAR or CES chord nowcasting, and its timing is far slower than real time.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Inputs are interpolated Te, Ti and density profiles, treated as observations at assimilation times. The target is the filtered state and short-term prediction. Diagnostic report latency is not addressed.
validation_if_relevant: Single shot with no untouched data. Hyperparameters were selected by likelihood on the same data.
forbidden_inferences: Do not state that it validates real-time capability or our 10 ms target.
Do not state that it concerns impurity CES or BES/ECEI.
Do not treat estimated C profiles as identified physics.
Do not generalize it to all prior work.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: At most an optional citation for the Kalman/data-assimilation concept in a theory aside. It does not address our task, baselines or diagnostics.
